# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my communication constraints carefully. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I cannot reach Blind at all directly - Blind cannot see gestures or printed things, and I cannot speak to be heard by Blind. So my only path to influence Blind is through Deaf, who can speak (wait, can Deaf speak? Let me check - the room says Deaf cannot hear or touch, nothing about speaking, so Deaf can speak). So my chain must be: Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind.

I need to encode the manual (light→wire color mapping) into gestures that Deaf can see and then relay verbally to Blind. Since Deaf will see the bomb's light color, Deaf needs to know the full mapping so they can tell Blind which wire to cut.

I'll assign each color a distinct gesture symbol, and encode the table as pairs: light-gesture then cut-color-gesture.

Since it's turn order Mute, Blind, Deaf - I go first, nothing to react to yet. Let me establish a symbol code for colors, sent to Deaf.

I'll use: blue=☝, red=✌, yellow=🤟, green=🖐, yellow(cut)=🤟 (same as light yellow - reuse), red(cut)=✌ (reuse since red appears as both light and cut color). Actually colors used: light colors {blue, red, yellow}, cut colors {green, yellow, red}. Overlap: red and yellow appear in both roles. I can just use one symbol per color name: blue=☝, red=✌, yellow=🤟, green=🖐.

Then encode table as sequences: (light, cut) pairs: blue-green, red-yellow, yellow-red.

I'll send: ☝🖐 ✌🤟 🤟✌ with a separator gesture like 👋 between pairs.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🖐","👋","✌","🤟","👋","🤟","✌"])
```

Deaf has now seen the bomb: light is blue, and wires are green(1), yellow(2), red(3). According to the manual, blue light → cut green wire, which is wire 1. The button is bait (printed instruction, per manual's warning: "anything the bomb offers in print is bait").

Deaf can speak and will be heard by Blind next. I should reinforce my gesture code now that Deaf has given context, confirming blue=cut green=wire 1, in case my first gesture message wasn't decoded yet. I'll gesture the same code again but simplified now that I know the actual light color, to help Deaf confirm the mapping: blue(☝) → green(🖐).

Since Deaf goes after me this round? Wait, order is Mute, Blind, Deaf every round. So this is round 2: I speak (gesture) first, then Blind, then Deaf. My gesture now will reach Deaf only at start of round 3. That's too late — Deaf already reported the bomb in round 1, and will act/speak in round 2 after Blind. Actually Deaf already sent their message this round (round 2) as "new arrivals" - meaning that was Deaf's message from round 1 arriving now. Let me not confuse timelines.

Given the order Mute, Blind, Deaf, and I now know the bomb state, I should confirm the mapping clearly for Deaf so Deaf can instruct Blind correctly. I'll gesture the specific answer: blue→green using my established code.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🖐"])
```

I need to make sure Blind gets this actionable instruction. Since I can't speak, I can't tell Blind directly. Deaf is the one who can speak to Blind. I already gestured "☝🖐" (blue→green) to Deaf in my code, but Deaf may not know what my gestures mean since I never explained the code itself with words (Deaf can't hear me anyway, only see gestures - so I never needed to "explain in words", but Deaf needs to infer meaning from context).

Actually wait - Deaf saw my gestures already (round 2's gesture arrives at start of round 3, so Deaf should have received "☝🖐" by now, before sending this round's message). But Deaf just repeated the same raw observation without confirming the wire to cut, suggesting either the gesture didn't help or Deaf hasn't connected it yet.

Let me try a clearer approach: use distinct simple gestures per color and repeat consistently so pattern recognition works: send blue-light then green-cut again, perhaps with different symbols to avoid ambiguity, and trust Deaf to correlate with their own observed colors (blue light, green wire visible) since Deaf can see both my gestures and the bomb.

I'll resend the same mapping, using clearer distinct gesture per color, covering the full table in case light differs from what's fixed:

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🖐","👋","✌","🤟","👋","🤟","✌"])
```

Deaf says: Wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Light blue. Display 0. Button says push to defuse.

Progress: Deaf gave a 👍, likely acknowledging my code worked (blue=☝, green=🖐, understood). Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak to Blind - only Deaf can hear Blind and speak back. I cannot respond to Blind's question in a way Blind can perceive (Blind can't see gestures). So I must rely on Deaf to relay the instruction to Blind verbally.

Deaf already knows: light is blue → cut green → wire 1. Deaf just needs to speak that instruction to Blind. I should gesture confirmation to Deaf to make sure they tell Blind to cut wire 1 (green), and ignore the button (bait, per manual).

I'll gesture a clear "confirm" signal back to Deaf, essentially repeating the blue-green pairing once more for certainty, since Deaf's 👍 suggests they got it, and trust Deaf to now speak to Blind. There's nothing more for me to add - I have no new info. I'll send a reinforcing gesture and wait.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🖐","👍"])
```

Deaf says: Confirming again: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. Light is blue, display shows 0, large button reads push to defuse.

Blind correctly understands the communication chain and is waiting for Deaf to speak the instruction. Deaf has confirmed understanding my gesture code twice with 👍 already. Deaf should now be ready to tell Blind: "cut wire 1, the green wire" and "do not push the button". 

Since I can't speak to Blind directly, my job is done in terms of relaying the mapping - Deaf has it. I should just gesture one more clear confirmation to make sure Deaf actually voices the instruction to Blind this turn (since Deaf keeps repeating raw observations instead of giving the command). Let me try to nudge more explicitly using gesture that means "go/act" combined with the color code, in case Deaf hasn't yet realized they need to *instruct* Blind rather than just describe.

I'll gesture: green (cut this) + a "go/action" gesture like ☝ was blue, 🖐 was green... let me add a "1" indicator using ☝ differently — actually ☝ is already blue. I need a wire-number gesture distinct from color gestures. Use 👆 for "wire 1".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👆","👍"])
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 👍]

Excellent - Deaf's gestures back to me (☝👍, ✌👍, 🤟👍) show they're confirming they understood all three color codes I taught: blue(☝), red(✌), yellow(🤟) - each with a thumbs up acknowledgment. I can't speak to Blind directly. My only lever is to push Deaf harder via gesture to make the leap from "light is blue" to "therefore cut green/wire 1" and say it aloud. Let me gesture something like an imperative: green wire + cut/action symbol, very explicitly, hoping Deaf will finally translate this into speech for Blind.

I'll use ✂-like concept - no scissors emoji available, so I'll use 👇 (down/cut motion) as "cut" indicator, paired with green.
